name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+15 district with a well-funded Democratic incumbent (about $2M raised plus outside support near $1M)
Opposition limited to independents and minor-party candidates with no visible fundraising
Polymarket prices a Democratic win near 95%, slightly below what fundamentals imply
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race
model.rationale: A D+15 Hudson County seat, Menendez's large financial edge, and an opposition field of unfunded independents all point to a comfortable Democratic hold; prediction markets price the race near 95 percent Democratic, a touch softer than fundamentals imply but still firmly in safe territory.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Menendez name materially eroding his support, or a challenger suddenly raising serious money, would be the main reason to revisit the rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Rob Menendez seeks reelection in a Hudson County-based district that leans Democratic by about fifteen points. He enters the general election with roughly $2 million raised and outside support approaching $1 million, while the field against him consists of independents and minor-party candidates with no visible fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency and money.

Prediction markets put Menendez's win probability near 95 percent, a touch below what the district's fundamentals alone would imply, leaving room for modest uncertainty. Even so, an underfunded opposition in a seat this Democratic makes an upset hard to construct. The forecast calls the race Safe Democratic, with Menendez favored by roughly twenty points.
